_about: Which AI plays which part in the Agent Room. Change a model here, then
run `python3 scripts/agentroom.py check` - it says whether each model
exists on OpenRouter and what a planning run can cost at most. A wrong
name is refused before a run starts, never discovered halfway through.
max_tokens is the most one reply may write; it is also what the money
check assumes a reply WILL write, so a bigger number reserves more of
the day's allowance per call. The money caps are not here: they are
agentroom_daily_ai and agentroom_run_max in tasks/limits.json, beside
the ecosystem's other caps.
Reasoning models (all three here) think before they answer, and the
thinking is billed as output and counts against max_tokens: on
2026-10-15 DeepSeek thought through all of 6000 and answered nothing.
Hence room to spare. Every call also goes to the cheapest host at
most 1.5x the listed price (or_chat.py PRICE_HEADROOM).
builder (owner, 2026-10-15): Claude Code on its OWN Claude login
(AGENTROOM_BUILDER_TOKEN), as the agentbuilder account in a sandbox, only
inside window, at most phases_per_night phases and sessions_per_night
sessions a night, and at most night_cap_usd of plan use a night as Claude
itself counts it at list prices. attempts: sessions a phase gets to pass.
bug_checker reads each phase's changes; watchdog (a different AI) reads
every session and HOLDS the build when anything looks wrong. Both are
paid, under agentroom_build_max in tasks/limits.json.
judge (owner, 2026-10-16): the second opinion. When the watchdog holds
for more than low concerns, it reads the same evidence; the build
waits for the owner only if it agrees, or its reply cannot be read.
Low-only concerns carry on, listed in the Room. Paid like the others.
app_ai (owner, 2026-10-19): the AI helper the built apps may ask, through
the sites server (POST <app>/_ai). Fast and cheap, as a person waits on
it. Capped by apps_daily_ai in tasks/limits.json, inside the key's
agentroom_daily_ai. The key never reaches the browser.
